- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below model output.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots downward — cap forecast decline to 10% below peak or align with 30-day moving average.  
- If sentiment is positive and price is falling, model often underreacts — increase forecast by 2–5% to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon — add 1–3% to forecast for first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–0.2+), model exhibits lag — delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to match sentiment momentum.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model tends to overcorrect — apply a 3–5% downward bias to forecast to avoid overbought correction.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses mean reversion — if price is above 30-day MA, reduce forecast by 2–4% to align with mean reversion bias.
